title: Error Bounds for Neutrosophic Period Estimation
content: Period estimation is a fundamental problem in signal processing, time-series analysis, oscillatory systems, and the study of approximately periodic phenomena. In many applica- tions, observations are not available as exact numerical values but are instead described by intervals reecting measurement uncertainty or incomplete information. This paper develops a deterministic framework for period estimation from interval-valued event times within the neutrosophic statistical perspective. We consider an approximately periodic sequence whose event times are represented by intervals. The midpoint of each interval is used to construct a least-squares estimator of the period. Explicit error bounds are established in terms of the interval radii and the number of observed events. We also derive weighted least-squares bounds, give conditions for identiability, and discuss the propagation of uncertainty to the estimated frequency. A numerical example illustrates the resulting bounds. The analysis distinguishes deterministic measurement uncertainty from random sampling variability. The proposed results provide veriable error guarantees under stated assumptions, rather than relying on unqualied claims of statistical superiority.
